title: Data surface URL filter chip shows a select field's raw option value (产品类别 = software) instead of its label
body:
## What happens

On the bare data surface `/:objectName/data?filter[...]` (ADR-0055), a URL filter chip on a **select** field shows the option's raw stored **value** instead of its **label**. In zh-CN the chip reads `产品类别 = software`, when the field's option label is `软件`. Every other place on the same screen (the grid cell, the field's filter panel, the dashboard the user came from) draws `软件`.

This is the screen a dashboard drill's **Open in list / 在列表中打开** lands on, so it is the normal path from any chart grouped by a select field, not a hand-typed URL.

## Repro (HotCRM, local dev, @objectstack 18.6.0)

- Open the **Product Catalog** dashboard (`product_catalog_dashboard`) → widget **top_products** (bar chart, dimension `category`, a select field on `crm_product`).
- Click the **软件** bar → the drill dialog lists the right products → **在列表中打开**.
- It navigates to `/crm_product/data?filter[list_price][null]=false&filter[category]=software`.
- The list itself is correct (6 rows). The chip row shows `标价 不为 null` (correct: prose through the operator key) and `产品类别 = software` (wrong: raw value).

## Where

- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/drillUrlFilters.ts` → `groupFilterChips`: the plain-equality branch returns `{ field, text }` with `text = String(comparand)`. Membership/negation operators also join the raw comparands with `comparand.map(String).join(', ')`.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectDataPage.tsx` (the chip row, around `filterChips.map(({ field, text, textKey }) => …)`): the field half goes through `fieldLabel(objectDef.name, field, field)`, but `text` is drawn bare. Nothing maps a comparand on a `select` / `multiselect` / `radio` field through the field's `options` (and the option-label translation the grid already uses).

## Expected

For a field that has `options`, each comparand in the chip is drawn as its option's (translated) label, the same text the grid cell shows for that value. A comparand that matches no option stays as the raw value, so a stale or hand-edited URL is still visible as what it is.

Boolean and lookup comparands probably want the same treatment (`Yes`/`No`, the referenced record's name) but are out of scope here.

## Why p1

The drill-to-list path is how users get from every chart grouped by a select field to the records behind it, and the one chip that tells them what they are looking at shows an internal code. In non-English locales it reads as a different language mid-sentence.
